\subsection*{Randomized --- BPLIn PCount: Results}

\begin{definition}[Fixed-choice machine]
\lean{Randomized.BPLInP.fixCoin}
\label{Randomized.BPLInP.fixCoin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols and let $b$ be
a Boolean choice. Define the machine obtained from $N$ by always using choice $b$ at
every transition; it has the same number of work tapes, states, and initial state as
$N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fixing a machine’s choice bit]
\lean{Randomized.BPLInP.stepWith_fixCoin}
\label{Randomized.BPLInP.stepWith_fixCoin}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPLInP.fixCoin, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let
$b,b'\in\{0,1\}$, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean input. For every configuration $C$ of
the machine obtained from $N$ by fixing its choice bit to $b$, the step of that fixed
machine using $b'$ agrees with the step of $N$ using $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Dynamic-programming value]
\lean{Randomized.BPLInP.dpVal}
\label{Randomized.BPLInP.dpVal}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Randomized.BPLInP.fixCoin, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a
Boolean string, and let $s,V$ be natural numbers. Define $D(t,c)$ for natural numbers
$t,c$ recursively: at $t=0$, it is $1$ if the encoding of $x,c,s$ belongs to the
machine’s accepting language and $0$ otherwise. At time $t+1$, sum over all $c'<V$ the
value $D(t,c')$ once for each of the two fixed-choice machines whose transition relation
takes encoded value $c$ to $c'$ within the specified bound.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Upper bound on dynamic-programming values]
\lean{Randomized.BPLInP.dpVal_le}
\label{Randomized.BPLInP.dpVal_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Randomized.BPLInP.dpVal, Randomized.BPLInP.fixCoin}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and
let $x,s,V,t,c$ be natural-number parameters, with $x$ a finite bit string. The
dynamic-programming value at depth $t$ and code $c$ is at most $(2V)^t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Run Stays Within the Space Window]
\lean{Randomized.BPLInP.inWin_run}
\label{Randomized.BPLInP.inWin_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.NDTM.runWith_take_inWindow}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean choices, let $x$ be a
bit string, and let $s$ be a natural number. Suppose there is a space bound
$\mathrm{sp}$ such that every choice-word run of $N$ on every input of length $n$ uses
at most $\mathrm{sp}(n)$ space, and suppose $\mathrm{sp}(|x|)\le s$. Then, for every
choice word $w$, the configuration reached by running $N$ on $x$ under $w$ has every
work-tape head at distance at most $s$ from the origin, and every work-tape cell at
distance greater than $s$ from the origin is blank.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Configuration core determined by its code]
\lean{Randomized.BPLInP.coreSum_eq_of_code_eq}
\label{Randomized.BPLInP.coreSum_eq_of_code_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.bits_cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.NDTM.coreSum}
\difficulty{2}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic machine over Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean
input, and let $s$ be a natural number. Suppose configurations $C$ and $D$ both have all
work-tape heads within distance $s$ of the origin and have blank tape cells at every
position of absolute value greater than $s$. If their configuration codes at radius $s$
are equal, then their cores agree: they have the same state, input-head position,
work-tape contents, work-tape head positions, and output summary (empty, exactly
$[\mathrm{true}]$, or no longer capable of becoming $[\mathrm{true}]$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of a Single Nondeterministic Step]
\lean{Randomized.BPLInP.stepRel_iff}
\label{Randomized.BPLInP.stepRel_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgWord_congr, Complexity.Codec.mem_stepLang, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Randomized.BPLInP.coreSum_eq_of_code_eq, Randomized.BPLInP.fixCoin, Randomized.BPLInP.inWin_run, Randomized.BPLInP.stepWith_fixCoin, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.NDTM.coreSum_stepWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.runWith_nil, Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let
$x$ and $v$ be bit strings, let $s$ and $c'$ be natural numbers, and let $b$ be a bit.
Suppose there is a function $sp$ from natural numbers to natural numbers such that $N$
uses at most $sp(n)$ space on inputs of length $n$, and suppose $sp(|x|)\le s$. Then the
encoded configuration reached by running the coin-fixed machine for $N$ on $x$ using
choice string $v$ has a step to the configuration encoded by $c'$ within the space
window $s$ if and only if $c'$ is the encoding of the configuration reached using choice
string $v$ followed by $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance language characterizes halting acceptance]
\lean{Randomized.BPLInP.acceptLang_iff}
\label{Randomized.BPLInP.acceptLang_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.mem_acceptLang, Randomized.BPLInP.coreSum_eq_of_code_eq, Randomized.BPLInP.inWin_run, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.outSummary_eq_accept_iff, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic machine over Boolean symbols, let $x$ and $v$ be
Boolean lists, and let $s$ be a natural number. Suppose $N$ uses space bounded by a
function $sp$ on every input, and $sp(|x|)\le s$. The encoding of $x$, the code of the
configuration reached by running $N$ on $x$ using choice string $v$, and the code of the
space bound $s$ belongs to the acceptance language of $N$ if and only if that run halts
and its output is exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized Acceptance Probability with No Coins]
\lean{Randomized.BPLInP.randProb_zero}
\label{Randomized.BPLInP.randProb_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.randProb}
\difficulty{3}
For every decidable predicate $A$ on bit strings, the probability that $A$ holds on a
uniformly random bit string of length zero equals $1$ if $A$ holds on the empty string,
and equals $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Dynamic-programming values and acceptance probability]
\lean{Randomized.BPLInP.dpVal_eq}
\label{Randomized.BPLInP.dpVal_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode_lt, Complexity.Codec.codeK, Complexity.logSpace, Randomized.BPLInP.acceptLang_iff, Randomized.BPLInP.dpVal, Randomized.BPLInP.fixCoin, Randomized.BPLInP.randProb_zero, Randomized.BPLInP.stepRel_iff, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_succ, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let
$x$ be a finite bit string, and let $s,V,t$ be natural numbers. Suppose there is a
function $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that on every input and every choice string,
the total number of work-tape cells visited by $N$ is at most $sp$ of the input length;
suppose also that $sp(|x|)\le s$ and $2^{K( s+\ell(|x|)+1)}\le V$, where $K$ is the
configuration-code constant of $N$ and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$. For every
natural number $t$ and every choice string $v$, the depth-$t$ dynamic-programming value
at the code of the configuration reached after choices $v$, viewed as a rational number,
equals $2^t$ times the probability that the machine, after choices $v$ followed by a
uniformly random Boolean string of length $t$, is halted and has output exactly the
one-bit string $[1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Halting within the code bound]
\lean{Randomized.BPLInP.haltsWithin_of_codes}
\label{Randomized.BPLInP.haltsWithin_of_codes}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode_lt, Complexity.Codec.codeK, Complexity.logSpace, Randomized.BPLInP.coreSum_eq_of_code_eq, Randomized.BPLInP.inWin_run, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin.mono, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.NDTM.coreSum_runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{7}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let
$x$ be a finite bit string, and let $s,V$ be natural numbers. Suppose there is a
function $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that on every input and every choice string,
the total number of work-tape cells visited by $N$ is at most $sp$ of the input length;
suppose $sp(|x|)\le s$ and $2^{K(s+\ell(|x|)+1)}\le V$, where $K$ is the

natural number $T$ such that every choice string of length $T$ makes $N$ halt on input
$x$, then every choice string of length $V$ also makes $N$ halt on input $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Initial dynamic-programming value]
\lean{Randomized.BPLInP.dpVal_init}
\label{Randomized.BPLInP.dpVal_init}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.codeK, Complexity.logSpace, Randomized.BPLInP.dpVal, Randomized.BPLInP.dpVal_eq, Randomized.BPLInP.haltsWithin_of_codes, Randomized.randProb_congr, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith_nil}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let
$x$ be a finite bit string, and let $s,V$ be natural numbers. Suppose there is a
function $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that on every input and every choice string,
the total number of work-tape cells visited by $N$ is at most $sp$ of the input length;
suppose $sp(|x|)\le s$ and $2^{K(s+\ell(|x|)+1)}\le V$, where $K$ is the
configuration-code constant of $N$ and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$. If there is a
natural number $T$ such that every choice string of length $T$ makes $N$ halt on input
$x$, then the depth-$V$ dynamic-programming value at the code of the initial
configuration, viewed as a rational number, equals $2^V$ times the probability that $N$
outputs exactly $[1]$ on input $x$ under a uniformly random choice string of length $V$.
\end{theorem}
